summary: Iter88 verified the two-admin approval rule for admin-filed attendance corrections end-to-end. Backend: 9/9 pytest pass covering (1) non-super admin POST /api/corrections -> {auto_approved:false, needs_second_admin:true}, doc has needs_second_admin=true/needs_super_admin=false/filed_by_id=<admin2>; (2) filer's own decide (approve + reject) returns 403 'another admin must approve or reject it'; (3) approve-all by filer SKIPS filer's own row (listed in errors); (4) another non-super admin can approve and attendance row is mutated (corrected=true, corrected_via=cid); (5) another non-super admin can reject with admin_note; (6) Super Admin can approve admin2-filed correction; (7) Super Admin's own on-behalf correction still auto-applies; (8) legacy-shape pending doc (needs_super_admin=True, no needs_second_admin, filed_by_admin_id=admin2) correctly routes through the two-admin rule — admin2=403, other non-super admin=200; (9) member archive queued by admin2 stays Super-Admin-only — other non-super admin gets 403 ('Only a Super Admin...'), super admin can approve. Frontend: /admin/approvals verified for admin2 shows the sky '2ND ADMIN' badge (data-testid=approvals-second-admin-badge-<id>) + 'Another admin approves' lock pill (approvals-own-lock-<id>) on their filed correction and NO approve-correction button; the archive row shows 'Super Admin only' lock (approvals-superadmin-lock-<id>). Super admin view also verified — same correction shows approve/reject actions.
critical_code_review_comments: corrections.py:_needs_second_admin treats a legacy row (needs_super_admin=True + entity_type=attendance + kind!=bulk_delete) as needing a second admin — correct for the migration, but doc the behaviour on the field or add a Mongo migration to also set needs_second_admin=true so audit-log readers see consistent flags.

approvals row — super admin sees 'approve' AND '2ND ADMIN' badge simultaneously. Fine, but consider dropping the badge (or re-labelling to 'admin-filed') once a super admin is viewing to reduce visual noise.

members.py:_queue_member_action does not stamp needs_second_admin=False explicitly on insert. Current frontend normCorrection treats these correctly (two_person=false because needs_super_admin=true + entity_type='member' falls through due to the attendance guard), but setting both flags on write would make the data self-describing.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (4/4 admin2 assertions: 2nd-admin-badge visible, own-lock pill visible, approve-correction button absent, super-admin-lock on archive visible) + super view confirms approve buttons present on both correction and archive

test_credentials: Super admin admin@attendance.app / Admin@12345; non-super admin2.test@example.com / Admin@12345 — the admin2 account was auto-created by the test fixture (mobile 9000000002, NOT in SUPER_ADMIN_PHONES default whitelist 9849002111).
seed_data_creation: Throwaway staff member 'TEST Throwaway Member' + 5 attendance rows (2025-12-10..16) and throwaway 'TEST Throwaway Admin' (role=admin, mobile 9000055xxx) + separate 'TEST Archive Target' member for the archive sub-test — all created and deleted by module-scoped fixtures. UI seed (TEST UI 84da39 + 1 attendance + 1 pending correction + 1 pending archive request) deleted via cleanup script. mongo users TEST_* count after cleanup = 0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression file /app/backend/tests/test_review_iter88.py is fully self-contained — creates its own admin2 if missing, creates throwaway non-super admin, seeds attendance via pymongo, and tears everything down. Uses /api/auth/me (not /api/me). The admin2 account persists in the preview DB with rules_accepted=true, so UI tests against admin2 should no longer be gated by the /rules redirect. Default SUPER_ADMIN_PHONES is '9849002111' when env is unset. The frontend testid grammar is approvals-approve-${kind}-${id} where kind='correction' for correction rows (matches review-request wording approvals-approve-correction-<id>).
rca of the issue: N/A — iter88 is a feature-verification pass of the newly introduced two-admin rule. Previous rule (super-admin-only for admin-filed attendance corrections) is intentionally obsolete; legacy rows carrying only needs_super_admin=True are retro-handled by _needs_second_admin() which treats them as two-person rows for attendance (verified in test_08).
